title: Policeman who wanted to throw his pay into the lake
summary: At a lake picnic job a city police sergeant tried to withhold or throw away the band's money until another man intervened.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I was playing on a job when he fell back off the camp and broke his leg. Really? Sergeant Morris, another one, he wanted to throw my money in the canal when I finished playing. Well there's always a good fellow in the crowd. I said, I come along and he said, why don't you have to invite them boys and play it all day for you? What you want to throw that money on in that lake? Put them caps on the water. If you'd thrown it down in the lake, you could look right down there, watch how clear that water was. You could look right down that water and see it. I've seen the water that's clear out there now, sometimes. It's going to make you die for him, huh?
Huh? It's going to make you die in the water for him.

Yeah, no you didn't have to die. You just have to come down on that step that's going in the water. Who wanted to do that? You didn't work for that money, it was yours. And so one good fellow come along, oh get them people that money, let them go home. Well, he finally paid off.
That was who did that? That was Sergeant Morris.
He wanted to do it, he didn't do anything.
That was a police force. Huh? On the police force. How did he relate to that? A sergeant? Was he a sergeant in the army?
No, no. City police. City police.
